taxon.note: Scientific and common names as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

allometry.note: 11 m at 30 years in the open, within the Flora of Guatemala's usual 8-12 m or more for grown trees. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

traits.life_span.note: Standley and Steyermark (1952), Flora of Guatemala III pp. 338-340, Hedyosmum mexicanum: trees, sometimes shrubs.

traits.leaf_habit.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as the Flora of Guatemala does not say.

traits.height_typical_m.note: Standley and Steyermark (1952), Flora of Guatemala III pp. 338-340, Hedyosmum mexicanum: very variable in size, often flowering as a 2 m shrub, but more commonly a tree of 8-12 m or more with a thick trunk and dense crown.

traits.height_max_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), above the Flora of Guatemala's "8-12 m or more".

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Standley and Steyermark (1952), Flora of Guatemala III pp. 338-340, Hedyosmum mexicanum: blades mostly 12-20 cm long and 3-6 cm wide.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Standley and Steyermark (1952), Flora of Guatemala III pp. 338-340, Hedyosmum mexicanum: blades mostly 12-20 cm long and 3-6 cm wide.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Standley and Steyermark (1952), Flora of Guatemala III pp. 338-340, Hedyosmum mexicanum: blades narrowly lanceolate or oblong-lanceolate, acuminate.

traits.inflorescence.note: Standley and Steyermark (1952), Flora of Guatemala III pp. 338-340, Hedyosmum mexicanum: male spikes cylindric and catkin-like; female flowers many, in a dense ovoid or subglobose head.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: Standley and Steyermark (1952), Flora of Guatemala III pp. 338-340, Hedyosmum mexicanum: male spikes 2-8 cm long, 5-8 mm thick.

traits.flower_colour.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as the Flora of Guatemala gives no colour; the anthers' pale yellow-green as the authors render it.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), for one drupe; the Flora of Guatemala gives the fruiting head, 2-3 cm long and 1.5-2 cm thick.

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: Standley and Steyermark (1952), Flora of Guatemala III pp. 338-340, Hedyosmum mexicanum: fruits very fleshy and juicy, whitish when ripe; the RGB is the authors' rendering.

traits.flowering_months.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as the Flora of Guatemala gives no months.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as the Flora of Guatemala gives no months.

traits.leaf_colour.note: A mid to dark green, the median over each photograph of its green, saturated pixels, then the median over the photographs, in 19 photographs in iNaturalist research-grade observations 7733707, 14081612, 18404648, 37256404, 74856600, 133534873, 196254464 (CC0, CC BY).

traits.bark_colour.note: A grey-brown trunk, the median of its pixels behind the foliage in observation 7733707; grey trunks and limbs too in 196254464.

traits.crown_form.note: Steeply ascending limbs from a straight trunk spread into a crown narrower below than above, its leaves crowded toward the shoot tips (observations 18404648, 196254464).

traits.self_pruning.note: Forest trees stand on tall straight trunks bare of limbs below the crown (observations 7733707, 18404648).

generator.params.crown_base.note: The crown starts about a third of the way up an 11-13 m tree, about 4 m, read by eye against the trunk in iNaturalist photographs (observations 18404648, 7733707).

generator.params.fork_height.note: The straight trunk forks into its ascending limbs about 3 m up, read by eye in the same photographs (observations 18404648, 7733707).

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy (Chloranthaceae, 2026-10-16): sizes and looks stated as facts from the Flora of Guatemala and drawn by the decurrent tree defaults and the angiosperm rules; leaf habit, greatest height, months and drupe size from the species-facts estimates.
